title: A Regiment for the Ledger
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, Jude Sterling has survived three years of indenture to the Corvane Trading Company by learning which silences keep people safe. When an infant is left at the company door with a note instructing her to forget its face, Jude recognizes the handwriting of Captain Ilya Marchetti—her late father's sworn friend, now declared an enemy of the crown and hunted for treason. Bound by a promise made years ago on her father's deathbed, Jude hides the child among the ledger clerks' families while unraveling why Marchetti trusted her, discovering that her own mother's pearl money helped finance his supposed betrayal. As the company's auditors close in and a bounty clerk begins matching faces to records, Jude must choose between the loyalty that kept her invisible and the truth that could free them both; in the end she trades the company's forged shipping ledgers for safe passage, sends the child to Marchetti's allies abroad, and signs her own name into the record for the first time—no longer invisible, but no longer owned.
about_author: Sable Almeida is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging port ledgers and indenture contracts along the old trade routes. Their fiction explores what ordinary record-keepers do with the truths entrusted to them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Silences
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A day in the Corvane counting-house establishes her careful invisibility: she reads ledgers faster than the clerks, notices discrepancies no one asks about, and keeps her diver's childhood hidden. Emotional beat: competence as camouflage, and the ache of being unseen even by those who rely on her.

chapters.title: Left at the Door
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Before dawn, a bundle appears on the company steps: an infant, a pearl on a cord, and a note in a hand Jude knows—Captain Marchetti's—instructing her to forget the face. She hides the child with the laundress Odile. Emotional beat: terror colliding with recognition; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What Father Promised
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with flashback. She recalls her father's deathbed bargain with Marchetti aboard the pearl boat: 'if ever my child can shelter yours, she will.' Now Marchetti is a declared traitor, and harboring his blood is treason. Emotional beat: the promise transforming from memory into obligation.

chapters.title: The Auditor Arrives
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and auditor Cassian Roe's POVs. Roe arrives to reconcile Corvane's books against crown seizures—and to hunt sympathizers of Marchetti. He notices Jude's unusual fluency with the ledgers. Emotional beat: the hunter's curiosity becoming a tightening noose.

chapters.title: Pearls in the Margin
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following ledger anomalies, Jude discovers entries her mother's pearl money funded—shipments later marked seized, evidence the company framed Marchetti to cover its own smuggling. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose; the enemy may be innocent.

chapters.title: A Name in the Registry
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Roe cross-references indenture registries and finds Jude Sterling listed as daughter of a drowned diver tied to Marchetti's crew. He confronts her gently, offering protection for testimony. Emotional beat: seduction of safety versus instinct that his kindness is a trap.

chapters.title: Odile's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The hiding network strains—a clerk's wife grows suspicious, the baby falls ill, and Odile demands Jude decide: give the child up or commit fully. Jude forges a burial entry to erase the child from company records. Emotional beat: first true act of rebellion; fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Sealed Hold
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Jude learns the original unaltered manifests sit in the company's sealed hold, proof of both Marchetti's innocence and her mother's unwitting complicity. Roe, closing in, searches the servants' quarters the same night. Emotional beat: two investigations converging on the same locked room.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Climax: caught copying the manifests, Jude bargains with Roe—not with silence, but with truth—exposing Corvane's directors while demanding passage for the child and clemency testimony for Marchetti. The director general's men intervene violently; Odile is hurt shielding the baby. Emotional beat: loyalty to persons finally outweighing loyalty to survival.

chapters.title: Signed in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue months later. The scandal breaks Corvane; Marchetti, cleared, comes ashore to claim his daughter—and finds Jude, indenture voided, keeping the girl until he arrives. She signs the transfer register in her own name, first time in the book. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed not as property but as identity; visibility chosen at last.
